la: {℟.} In monte Olivéti orávit ad Patrem: Pater, si fíeri potest, tránseat a me calix iste: Spíritus quidem promptus est, caro autem infírma: * Fiat volúntas tua. {℣.} Verúmtamen non sicut ego volo, sed sicut tu vis. * Fiat.
en: {℟.} On the Mount of Olives he prayed to the Father: Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak: * Thy will be done. {℣.} Nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. * Thy will.

la: {℟.} Tristis est ánima mea usque ad mortem: sustinéte hic, et vigiláte mecum: nunc vidébitis turbam, quæ circúmdabit me: * Vos fugam capiétis, et ego vadam immolári pro vobis. {℣.} Ecce appropínquat hora, et Fílius hóminis tradétur in manus peccatórum. * Vos fugam.
en: {℟.} My soul is sorrowful even unto death: stay here and watch with me: now you shall see the crowd that will surround me: * You will take flight, and I shall go to be sacrificed for you. {℣.} Behold the hour is at hand, and the Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of sinners. * You will take flight.

la: {℟.} Ecce vídimus eum non habéntem spéciem, neque decórem: aspéctus ejus in eo non est. Hic peccáta nostra portávit, et pro nobis dolet: ipse autem vulnerátus est propter iniquitátes nostras: * Cujus livóre sanáti sumus. {℣.} Vere languóres nostros ipse tulit, et dolóres nostros ipse portávit. * Cujus.
en: {℟.} Behold, we have seen him without form or comeliness: there is no beauty in him. He has borne our sins and grieves for us; but he was wounded for our iniquities: * By whose bruises we are healed. {℣.} Surely he hath borne our infirmities, and carried our sorrows. * By whose bruises.

la: {℟.} Amícus meus ósculi me trádidit signo. Quem osculátus fúero, ipse est, tenéte eum. Hoc malum fecit signum, qui per ósculum adimplévit homicídium. * Infélix prætermísit prétium sánguinis, et in fine láqueo se suspéndit. {℣.} Fílius quidem hóminis vadit, sicut scriptum est de illo: væ autem hómini illi, per quem tradétur. * Infélix.
en: {℟.} My friend betrayed me by the sign of a kiss: Whom I shall kiss, that is he: hold him fast. He who committed murder by a kiss gave this wicked sign. * The unhappy man cast away the price of blood, and in the end hanged himself. {℣.} The Son of man indeed goes, as it is written of him; but woe to that man by whom he shall be betrayed. * The unhappy man.

la: {℟.} Unus ex vobis tradet me hódie: væ illi, per quem tradar ego: * Mélius illi erat, si natus non fuísset. {℣.} Qui intíngit mecum manum in parópside, hic me traditúrus est in manus peccatórum. * Mélius.
en: {℟.} One of you will betray me today: woe to him by whom I shall be betrayed: * It were better for him if he had not been born. {℣.} He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, he will betray me into the hands of sinners. * It were better.

la: {℟.} Eram quasi agnus ínnocens: ductus sum ad immolándum, et nesciébam: consílium fecérunt inimíci mei advérsum me, dicéntes: * Veníte, mittámus lignum in panem ejus, et eradámus eum de terra vivéntium. {℣.} Omnes inimíci mei advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi: verbum iníquum mandavérunt advérsum me, dicéntes. * Veníte.
en: {℟.} I was like an innocent lamb: I was led to be sacrificed, and I knew it not: my enemies took counsel against me, saying: * Come, let us put wood into his bread, and cut him off from the land of the living. {℣.} All my enemies devised evils against me: they uttered a wicked word against me, saying. * Come.

la: {℟.} Una hora non potuístis vigiláre mecum, qui exhortabámini mori pro me? * Vel Judam non vidétis, quómodo non dormit, sed festínat trádere me Judǽis? {℣.} Dormíte jam, et requiéscite: ecce appropínquat, qui me tradet. * Vel Judam.
en: {℟.} Could you not watch one hour with me, you who urged one another to die for me? * Or do you not see Judas, how he sleeps not, but hastens to betray me to the Jews? {℣.} Sleep now and take your rest: behold, he is at hand that will betray me. * Or do you not see Judas.

la: {℟.} Senióres pópuli consílium fecérunt, * Ut Jesum dolo tenérent, et occíderent: cum gládiis, et fústibus exiérunt tamquam ad latrónem. {℣.} Collegérunt ergo Pontífices et Pharisǽi concílium. * Ut Jesum.
en: {℟.} The elders of the people took counsel, * That they might take Jesus by guile and put him to death: they went out as against a robber, with swords and clubs. {℣.} The chief priests and the Pharisees therefore gathered a council. * That they might take.

la: {℟.} Revelábunt cæli iniquitátem Judæ, et terra advérsus eum consúrget: et maniféstum erit peccátum illíus in die furóris Dómini: * Cum eis, qui dixérunt Dómino Deo: Recéde a nobis, sciéntiam viárum tuárum nólumus. {℣.} In diem perditiónis servábitur, et ad diem ultiónis ducétur. * Cum eis.
en: {℟.} The heavens shall reveal the iniquity of Judas, and the earth shall rise up against him: and his sin shall be made manifest in the day of the Lord's wrath: * With those who said to the Lord God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways. {℣.} He shall be kept for the day of destruction, and shall be led to the day of vengeance. * With those.
